title.en: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle

text.en: A ladder leans against a wall. Its steepness depends on the angle it makes with the ground. Trigonometry gives the steepness as a ratio.

In a right triangle the side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. For an angle θ, the side opposite θ is the opposite side and the other side is the adjacent side.
The three main ratios are sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent. A memory aid is SOH CAH TOA.
For a 3, 4, 5 right triangle and the angle opposite the side 3 we get sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5 and tan θ = 3/4. The reciprocals are cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ and cot θ = 1/tan θ.
Some values to remember are sin 30° = 1/2, cos 60° = 1/2, sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2 and tan 45° = 1. Also sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for every angle.

problem.en: In a right triangle, the opposite side is 5 and the hypotenuse is 13. Find the adjacent side, sin θ, cos θ and tan θ.

text.en: Adjacent² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the adjacent side is 12.

prompt.en: A friend says sin θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Remember SOH: sine is opposite over hypotenuse

points.en: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent.
